newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Hills rated a buy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT-Hills rated a buy.

text.p: Broker Day Cutten Ltd has issued a buy recommendation for metal and electronic products maker Hills Industries Ltd, saying the stock, A$7.05 at the time of writing, was too heavily discounted to industrial benchmarks.

Analyst Roly Michelmore said in a report that earnings growth was expected to bottom in the current year as demand for products in the consumer products division passed through the trough of the housing downturn.

Good growth prospects for the electronics division, with additional potential upside from pay TV developments and leverage to a housing recovery, were expected to drive earnings growth higher in 1997/98 to June 30, the report said.

Michelmore forecast net profit before abnormals to rise on flat sales through improving earnings before interest and tax margins, to A$12.6 million in 1996/97 from A$12.2 million the previous year, and further to A$13.5 million in 1997/98.
Sales were expected to rise to A$354 million in 1997/98 from an anticipated A$338 million in 1996/97, he said in Day Cutten's annual South Australian Companies Review, published this week.

The report said the discount to the industrial average price earnings ratio (PE), excluding banks, was 22 percent on Hill's prospective 1997/98 PE of 11.1 when a 10 percent discount was sufficient to adjust cyclical and other risks to earnings.

The report said sales for Hills' consumer products division were expected to remain flat in 1996/97, with no significant change anticipated until well into 1997/98 when only slow improvement was expected.
Margins had contracted sharply due to competing low specficiation products and increasing concentration of retail markets in the large chain stores, Michelmore said.

Improved demand was expected in 1997/98 in the industrial products division, as housing and commercial building activity were resurrected and continuing expansion into precision metal products would be positive for revenue and margins, he said.
He forecast six to eight percent annual revenue growth for the next two years for the electronics division, with improving margins as the emphasis in pay TV changed from wholesaling to manufacture.

Michelmore said Hills had identified the relative illiquidity of the market in the company's securities as a barrier to maximum shareholder value and was taking two measures to encourage a more active and liquid market.

These were a 5-for-1 share split, approved by shareholders at the company's annual meeting last month, and an intention to raise the market capitalisation in the medium term to more than A$300 million by growth and acqusitions, he said.
Hills shares closed at A$1.81 on Tuesday, up six cents.
